slides.title: Two Ways to Combine Queries
slides.body: Merge combines two queries side-by-side — like a SQL JOIN, it adds new columns. Append stacks queries on top of each other — like a SQL UNION ALL, it adds more rows.
slides.keyPoint: Merge = more columns (lookup/enrich). Append = more rows (consolidate). Choose based on what your data shape needs.

slides.title: Merge — Enrich Orders with Customer Data
slides.note: Merge added Name and Region columns — row count stays the same (3 orders in, 3 orders out)

options.label: Merge
options.description: Combine horizontally by matching on a key column. Use to look up and add related data from another table.
pros: Adds columns from a related/lookup table
Supports Left / Right / Full / Inner join types
Equivalent to VLOOKUP or SQL JOIN

options.label: Append
options.description: Stack tables vertically. Use to consolidate data from multiple sources that share the same structure.
pros: Adds more rows of the same type of data
Use for multi-sheet, multi-file, or multi-period consolidation
